summary:
Starlight Quest is a 3D sci-fi adventure and action-quest game that I built in Unreal Engine 4 for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. In the game, the player takes on the role of a stranded astronaut who must explore Mars, complete planetary quests to buy a new spaceship engine, and travel to Jupiter to defend the sector against hostile aliens.
This project solves the challenge of making space exploration engaging and interactive rather than passive. Instead of simple single-level shooting, I combined quest-based progression, ship repairs, AI alien combat, and atmospheric space audio into one cohesive story. It matters because it gives students and sci-fi fans a fun, accessible way to experience space missions while sparking curiosity about Mars and Jupiter exploration.
details:
How It Works & Gameplay
Starlight Quest is a 3D sci-fi action-adventure game where the player steps into the role of an astronaut stranded on Mars. The gameplay is divided into two main planetary stages:

  • Level 1 (Mars): Players explore a rusty-red Martian landscape, collect scattered coins and crystals to earn currency, and purchase a new engine to repair their spaceship.
  • Level 2 (Jupiter): After unlocking the next stage via the level select menu, players travel to Jupiter's sector, where they must use a blaster to defeat four hostile aliens with custom AI navigation before completing the mission.

Key Benefits & Expected Impact
Unlike simple single-level arcade shooters, Starlight Quest combines resource collection, ship repairs, health management, and multi-planet exploration into one cohesive narrative. The game helps students and sci-fi fans experience space missions in a fun, accessible way while sparking curiosity about real planetary environments like Mars and Jupiter.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Engine & Scripting: Unreal Engine 4 and Blueprints Visual Scripting for gameplay logic, coin and crystal pickup systems, enemy AI movement (NavMesh & AI MoveTo), damage systems, and level transitions.
  • UI & Audio: Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG) for the main menu, level select screen, HUD health bar, currency counter, and win/loss screens, paired with persistent background space audio (GameInstance).
  • Deployment: Packaged into a standalone Windows 64-bit executable build so anyone can play without installing Unreal Engine.

Creativity & Design Considerations
To make the game intuitive and atmospheric, I focused on clear visual contrast between the red terrain of Mars and the cosmic skies of Jupiter, responsive player controls, and seamless audio continuity across levels. I also designed clear win and game-over states ("Mission Complete" and "You Died") so players always get immediate feedback on their progress.
